key_insight: The paper argues that robot policies become more capable when they reason directly in 3D geometry instead of relying only on 2D image features or latent representations. By explicitly modeling how objects, cameras, and robot actions interact in space, the policy can better handle contact-rich manipulation.
problem_solved: Existing vision-language-action and video world-action models understand semantics and motion well, but they often miss the 3D geometric relationships needed for precise robotic manipulation. This paper addresses the gap between 2D perception and the spatial reasoning required for real-world robot control.
method: Introduces a Geometric Action Model that incorporates 3D spatial structure into robot policy learning.
Connects object, camera, and robot-action interactions in a geometry-aware representation rather than relying only on 2D frames.
Targets contact-rich manipulation tasks where accurate spatial reasoning is critical for action selection and execution.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a path toward more reliable generalist robot policies that are both semantically informed and physically grounded. It may improve robustness on tasks requiring precise positioning, contact, and object interaction in complex environments.
visual_elements: A 3-panel diagram comparing 2D frame-based policies vs 3D geometry-aware policies
An interaction graph showing relationships among camera, object, and robot action
A before-and-after illustration of a manipulation task highlighting improved contact precision
A simplified 3D coordinate scene with trajectories, grasp points, and action vectors
paper_title: Geometric Action Model for Robot Policy Learning
paper_authors: Jisang Han, Seonghu Jeon, Jaewoo Jung, René Zurbrügg, Honggyu An
